title: Percolation on the hat tiling
words: Each hat tile is open at random with probability p. Find where an infinite open cluster first appears.
math: For site percolation on the hat adjacency graph, prove $0.6<p_c<0.7$ (or the correct interval) with rigorous bounds.

title: Hyperbolic Hex
words: On a board tiled by heptagons in hyperbolic space, find an explicit first-player win for Hex-like connection.
math: On the $(7,3)$ tiling with a disk of radius $r$ split into four boundary arcs, give an explicit winning strategy for the first player for all $r$.

title: Keller maps of degree 4
words: Show that every 3D polynomial map of degree at most 4 with constant Jacobian has a polynomial inverse.
math: Prove $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$, $\deg F\le4$, $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ implies $F$ is an automorphism.

title: Spectre Rupert
words: Extrude a spectre into a prism. Can a copy pass through a hole in itself?
math: Decide whether the right prism over the spectre of height 1 has the Rupert property.

title: Reverse-square orbits
words: Decide for every starting number whether squaring and reversing eventually loops.
math: Give an algorithm that decides, for every $n$, whether the $R$-orbit of $n$ is eventually periodic, with proof.

title: SOF Collatz orbits are bounded
words: For the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map, show no orbit runs off to infinity.
math: Prove $\sup_k g^k(n)<\infty$ for every $n$.

title: Car-like sofa
words: The sofa moves like a car: forward only, with limited steering. Find the biggest that makes the corner.
math: Maximize area over shapes whose motion is a forward Dubins path with turning radius $\ge1$ through the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Navier–Stokes blow-up in Isabelle
words: Re-check the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up in a completely different proof assistant.
math: Formalize in Isabelle/HOL the existence of a smooth forced finite-time blow-up of 3D Navier–Stokes.

title: Prime and square neighbours
words: Order all positive integers so neighbours add to a prime and numbers two apart add to a square.
math: Decide whether there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi_i+\pi_{i+1}$ prime and $\pi_i+\pi_{i+2}$ square for all $i$.

title: Hinged sofa
words: A sofa made of two rigid halves joined by a hinge. What total area can turn the corner?
math: Maximize $|A|+|B|$ for planar sets $A,B$ joined at a common point, moving with relative rotation allowed, through the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Hat graph is Hamiltonian
words: Show you can walk through every tile of any big hat-tiled region exactly once.
math: Prove every finite simply connected patch of a hat tiling has a Hamiltonian path in its adjacency graph.

title: Hyperbolic Kakeya in the plane
words: In the hyperbolic plane, the smallest set holding a unit segment in every direction should have zero area.
math: Construct a Lebesgue-null set in $\mathbb{H}^2$ containing a geodesic segment of length 1 in every direction, and determine the minimal Minkowski dimension of such sets.

title: Optimal sofa is not algebraic anywhere
words: Show the optimal sofa for a 60° turn has an outline that no polynomial equation describes.
math: Prove the boundary of the optimal sofa for the $60^\circ$ corridor contains no arc of any algebraic curve.

title: Lorenz attractor dimension
words: Pin down the fractal dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor to two decimals, rigorously.
math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $2.06\le\dim_H\mathcal{A}\le2.07$.

title: Prime-length pancakes, lower bound
words: Sort a stack of pancakes by flipping only a prime number of them at a time. Show you sometimes need noticeably more than n flips.
math: With prefix reversals of prime length only, show the worst-case sorting distance on $n$ pancakes is at least $n+c\log n$ for some $c>0$.

title: Seven-free primes in progressions
words: Primes avoiding the digit 7 should be evenly spread among remainder classes.
math: Prove primes without decimal digit 7 are equidistributed in residue classes mod $q$ for all $q\le(\log x)^A$.

title: Kakeya for spectres
words: Make a set that contains a spectre in every rotation but has zero area. Find its smallest possible dimension.
math: Determine the minimal Hausdorff dimension of a compact set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing a rotated copy of the spectre boundary at every angle.

title: Divisor-balanced primes
words: Show infinitely many primes p have p − 1 and p + 1 with the same number of divisors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $d(p-1)=d(p+1)$.

title: Spectre Ising criticality
words: Show magnets on a spectre tiling and on a hat tiling share the same critical temperature after rescaling by average neighbour count.
math: Prove or disprove $\beta_c(\text{spectre})\cdot\bar d_{\text{spectre}}=\beta_c(\text{hat})\cdot\bar d_{\text{hat}}$, where $\bar d$ is mean degree.

title: Doubled twins are infinite
words: Show infinitely many primes p have p + 2, 2p + 1 and 2p + 3 all prime.
math: Prove infinitely many $p$ with $p,p+2,2p+1,2p+3$ prime.

title: Small gap, then a huge one
words: Find infinitely many spots where a prime gap is at least the square of the gap before it.
math: Prove $p_{n+1}-p_n\ge(p_n-p_{n-1})^2$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Prime-frequency synchrony
words: Oscillators with frequencies set by logarithms of primes eventually synchronize when coupled strongly enough. Find the threshold.
math: For the Kuramoto model with $\omega_i=\log p_i$, prove a sharp synchronization threshold $K_c(N)$ and its asymptotics.

title: Random polykites
words: Show almost no shapes made of many kites can tile the plane.
math: Prove the fraction of $k$-kite polykites that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ decays exponentially in $k$.

title: Integer-bijective Keller map
words: Find a polynomial map with Jacobian 1 that shuffles integer points perfectly but has no polynomial inverse.
math: Find $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x]^n$, $\det DF\equiv1$, inducing a bijection of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ but not a polynomial automorphism.

title: Prime Nim is periodic in base 2
words: Show the Grundy values of Prime Nim follow a pattern that a finite machine reads off the binary digits, or prove none exists.
math: Decide whether the Grundy function of Prime Nim is $2$-automatic.

title: 5n+1 largest-factor cycles
words: Use 5n + 1 instead of 3n + 1 in the largest-factor map. Show it has only finitely many loops.
math: For $f_5(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(5n+1)$ (odd), prove $f_5$ has finitely many cycles.

title: Wind-blown fire fronts
words: A fire pushed by steady wind should end up with a convex, stable front shape.
math: For front speed $a+b\,|n\cdot w|$, prove every compact initial front becomes convex in finite time and converges in shape to the Wulff shape.

title: Hyperbolic Prime Nim
words: Prime Nim on a hyperbolic tree board. Decide who wins.
math: On the $(3,7)$ hyperbolic tiling graph, players move a token by a geodesic distance that is prime; the last mover wins. Determine the winner from any vertex.

title: Spiral staircase
words: What is the biggest convex box-like object that can be carried up a given spiral staircase?
math: Maximize volume over convex bodies admissible in a helical tube of square cross-section $1$, radius $2$, pitch $3$.

title: Fire spotting threshold
words: Embers jump ahead of a fire. Find the jump probability where firefighting becomes hopeless.
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, a burning cell also ignites a uniformly random cell at distance $\le r$ with probability $q$. Find $q^*(r,k)$ beyond which $k$ protections per turn fail a.s.

title: Vorticity growth in a hat
words: Fluid in a hat-shaped container should develop sharper and sharper swirls near its corners.
math: For 2D Euler in the hat polygon, prove $\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_\infty$ grows double exponentially for some smooth initial data.

title: Hat dominating sets
words: Find the smallest fraction of hat tiles that touch every other tile.
math: Compute the asymptotic domination density of the hat adjacency graph.

title: Five colors for square sums
words: Square-sum graphs need four colors eventually. Do they eventually need five?
math: Decide whether $\chi(S_N)\ge5$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Cube-sum paths
words: Arrange 1 to N in a line so neighbours add to perfect cubes, for every large N.
math: Prove $C_N$ has a Hamiltonian path for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Chess on the hat board
words: Solve a chess-like game on a hat-tiled board with 10 pieces per side.
math: Weakly solve the game with standard chess move semantics translated to the hat graph on a fixed 64-tile patch.

title: Square-sum Hamilton decomposition
words: Split all square-sum links into separate tours that each visit every number once.
math: Decide for which $N$ the square-sum graph (restricted to a regular spanning subgraph) admits a Hamiltonian decomposition, and prove it for infinitely many $N$.

title: Equal shuffle orders
words: For which deck sizes do the in-shuffle and the out-shuffle take the same number of repetitions?
math: Characterize all $n$ with $\operatorname{ord}_{2n+1}(2)=\operatorname{ord}_{2n-1}(2)$, and list those with $n\le10^6$.

title: Palindromic Carmichael numbers
words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers read the same backwards.
math: Prove there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers that are decimal palindromes.

title: Kissing spectres
words: How many spectre tiles can touch one spectre without overlapping?
math: Determine the maximal number of interior-disjoint congruent spectres meeting a fixed one.

title: Adversarial 2048
words: An opponent places every new tile in 2048 as unhelpfully as possible. What is the biggest tile you can still guarantee?
math: On the $4\times4$ board where an adversary chooses each spawn's position and value in $\{2,4\}$, determine the largest tile the player can force.

title: Petersen Ramsey multiplicity
words: In any two-coloring of a huge complete graph, how many single-color copies of the Petersen graph must appear, at least?
math: Determine the Ramsey multiplicity constant $\lim_n \min_{\text{2-col}} \#\text{mono } P / \#P \text{ in } K_n$ for the Petersen graph $P$.

title: S and Z Tetris
words: If only the S and Z pieces ever come, how many lines can you clear before losing on a 10-wide board?
math: On a $10\times20$ Tetris well with an adversarial sequence from $\{S,Z\}$, determine the maximum number of lines the player can guarantee.

title: Primes a² + b⁴ with prime inputs
words: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a fourth power of a prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^4$ with $p,q$ prime.

title: Firefighter on the hat tiling
words: Find the exact average number of firefighters per turn needed to contain any fire on a hat tiling.
math: Determine $\inf\{f: f\text{ firefighters per turn (averaged) contain every finite fire on the hat graph}\}$.

title: Smallest-factor Collatz stopping time
words: How many steps does the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map take to reach 1, on average?
math: Determine the asymptotic order of $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T_g(n)$ for the stopping time of $g$.

title: Largest-factor Collatz, almost always
words: For the largest-factor Collatz map, show that almost every starting number eventually drops below where it began.
math: For $f$ as above, prove $\{n: \exists k,\ f^k(n)<n\}$ has natural density $1$.

title: Constant-definition detector
words: Some proofs hide a definition that is secretly always true. Give a tool that finds such definitions automatically.
math: Give a sound procedure that, for a Lean 4 proof term, flags every definition on its dependency path that is provably constant, and prove it complete for propositional constants.

title: Fluid in a box blows up
words: Show viscous fluid in a closed box with sticky walls can blow up under a smooth push.
math: Construct smooth $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes with no-slip in the unit cube blows up in finite time.

title: Hat ground state
words: Find the arrangement of hat tiles that minimises a natural energy, and show it is the aperiodic tiling.
math: Prove the hat tiling is the unique (up to isometry) ground state of a finite-range two-body potential on hat-shaped particles in the plane.

title: Seven-free almost-Sophie-Germain
words: Show infinitely many primes p avoid the digit 7 and have 2p + 1 with few prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ have $\Omega(2p+1)\le3$.

title: Four colors, compressed
words: Make the computer-checked four color theorem much shorter.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the four color theorem in under 20,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Hyperbolic Sudoku
words: Play Sudoku on a hyperbolic tiling with heptagons. Find the fewest clues for a unique solution on the smallest board.
math: For the 7-colouring constraint problem on the Klein quartic's 24 heptagons (each heptagon and its 7 neighbours distinct where required), find the minimum number of givens for uniqueness.

title: Square-sum genus
words: How tangled is the square-sum graph? Show the number of handles needed to draw it grows linearly.
math: Prove $\operatorname{genus}(S_N)=\Theta(N)$ and determine all $N$ for which $S_N$ is planar.

title: Monotile in a strip
words: Find a tile that can fill an infinite strip only in a non-repeating way.
math: Find a connected tile tiling the strip $\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]$ only non-periodically, or prove none exists.

title: Rupert's Johnson solids
words: Decide which of the 92 Johnson solids can pass a copy of themselves through a hole in themselves.
math: For each Johnson solid $J$, decide whether some congruent copy of $J$ passes through a straight hole in $J$.

title: Polykite complete classification
words: For every polykite, decide whether it tiles, and if so how.
math: Give an algorithm deciding, for any single polykite, whether it tiles the plane, and prove it correct.

title: Fire on a random planet
words: Fire spreads on a random planar map. Find how fast firefighting budgets must grow.
math: On the uniform infinite planar triangulation, determine the minimal growth exponent $a$ such that budgets $k_t=t^{a}$ contain a fire almost surely.

title: Mathieu puzzle
words: Design a logic puzzle under ten thousand cells whose symmetries form exactly the Mathieu group M₂₄.
math: Find a finite constraint puzzle with $<10^4$ cells whose solution-preserving symmetry group is isomorphic to $M_{24}$.

title: Hat corona limit shape is not polygonal
words: Show the limiting shape of hat layers has a fractal outline.
math: Prove the limit shape of scaled hat coronas has boundary of Hausdorff dimension $>1$.

title: Random Keller maps
words: Show that a random polynomial map with constant Jacobian, in a natural model, is almost never invertible.
math: In the space of degree-$\le d$ Keller maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$, prove non-invertible ones form a Zariski-dense subset for $d\ge7$.

title: Graceful spider forests
words: Spiders are trees with one central branching vertex. Show forests of spiders have the distinct-difference labeling.
math: For any forest of spiders with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Readable Unique Games
words: The 2026 AI proof of the Unique Games Conjecture is nearly unreadable. Write one a human can follow.
math: Give a human-verifiable proof of the Unique Games Conjecture of at most 50 pages.

title: Fire on the triangular lattice
words: On a grid of triangles, fire spreads to all six neighbours. How few firefighters per turn can trap a single fire?
math: On the triangular lattice, find the least $k$ such that protecting $k$ cells per turn always contains a fire started at one vertex.

title: Small Hadwiger counterexample
words: The claimed counterexamples to Hadwiger's conjecture are astronomically large. Find one under a million vertices.
math: Find $G$ with $|V(G)|<10^6$ and $h(G)<\chi(G)$, or prove every counterexample is larger.

title: Keller maps over finite fields
words: Count the polynomial maps of three variables over a finite field with constant Jacobian that happen to be bijections.
math: For $F\in\mathbb{F}_p[x,y,z]^3$ of degree $\le3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times$, find the asymptotic proportion inducing bijections of $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ as $p\to\infty$.

title: Trees inside square sums
words: Show the square-sum graph contains every small tree as a subgraph.
math: Prove $S_N$ contains every tree on at most $c\log N$ vertices, for some $c>0$.

title: Sofa angle monotonicity
words: As a hallway's turn gets sharper, the best sofa should get smaller. Prove it between 60° and 90°.
math: Let $A(\theta)$ be the maximal sofa area for a width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$. Prove $A$ is decreasing on $[\pi/3,\pi/2]$.

title: LF-Collatz loops classified forever
words: Show every largest-factor Collatz-type map for every odd multiplier has only finitely many loops, with a uniform recipe.
math: For every odd $a\ge3$, prove $f_a(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(an+1)$ (odd) has finitely many cycles, with an explicit bound in $a$.

title: After the blow-up
words: Once the 2026 Navier–Stokes solution blows up, show there is exactly one sensible way to continue it.
math: Prove uniqueness of Leray–Hopf continuations past the 2026 forced blow-up time.

title: Asymptotic freedom, rigorously
words: Show the 2026 rigorous QCD behaves freely at short distances, as physicists expect.
math: Prove the correlation functions of the 2026 QCD construction satisfy the asymptotic-freedom scaling of the one-loop beta function.

title: FLT, compressed
words: Fermat's Last Theorem has a huge computer formalization effort. Do it in far fewer lines.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of $x^n+y^n=z^n\Rightarrow xyz=0$ for $n\ge3$ using at most $10^5$ lines beyond current Mathlib.

title: Coloring the hat tiling
words: Color the tiles of a hat tiling so that touching tiles differ. Are three colors enough?
math: Decide whether the adjacency graph of every hat tiling is 3-colourable.

title: Twin hats
words: Find a pair of different tiles that can each tile the plane only together, aperiodically, with a matching rule nobody has found yet.
math: Find two polykites $A,B$ with $\le 6$ kites each, neither tiling alone, that together tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ only aperiodically.

title: 3-pile shuffle mixing constant
words: Find the exact cutoff constant for riffle-style 3-pile shuffles, in closed form.
math: For random 3-pile shuffles on $3n$ cards, prove cutoff at $c\log n$ with $c$ in closed form and window $O(1)$.

title: Anti-knight Sudoku
words: In this Sudoku, equal digits may not sit a knight's move apart. What is the fewest clues for a unique solution?
math: Determine the minimum number of givens in a uniquely solvable $9\times9$ Sudoku with the extra anti-knight constraint.

title: Zigzag sofa
words: A hallway turns right, then left after distance d. Find the best sofa for every d.
math: For each $d>0$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with two opposite right turns separated by $d$.

title: Twelve-tone Ramsey
words: Any long enough melody must contain a repeated interval pattern. Find how long.
math: Find the least $L$ such that every sequence in $\mathbb{Z}_{12}^L$ contains two disjoint consecutive blocks of length 4 with equal interval vectors.

title: Voice leading is NP-hard
words: Moving n voices through a chord progression with the least total motion while avoiding parallel fifths should be computationally hard.
math: Show NP-hardness of minimizing $\sum_t\sum_i |x_{t+1,i}-x_{t,i}|$ over voicings of a given chord sequence with $n$ voices, subject to no parallel perfect fifths.

title: Square-sum spectral gap
words: Find how well connected the square-sum graph is, through its eigenvalues.
math: Determine the asymptotics of $\lambda_1(S_N)-\lambda_2(S_N)$ for the adjacency spectrum.

title: First-click Minesweeper
words: On a beginner Minesweeper board, what is the chance your guaranteed-safe first click opens at least ten squares?
math: On a $9\times9$ board with 10 mines placed uniformly avoiding the first click, compute exactly $\Pr(\text{revealed region}\ge10)$, maximized over the click position.

title: Carmichael numbers of one type
words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers use only primes that leave remainder 1 when divided by 4.
math: Prove there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers all of whose prime factors are $\equiv1\pmod4$.

title: Hat spectrum is a Cantor set
words: Show the energy levels of a particle hopping on a hat tiling form a dust of measure zero.
math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the hat graph is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Mod-3 Collatz map
words: Divide by 3 when you can; otherwise double and add or subtract 1. Find all loops below a billion.
math: Let $h(n)=n/3$ if $3\mid n$, $2n+1$ if $n\equiv1$, $2n-1$ if $n\equiv2 \pmod 3$. Classify all cycles of $h$ meeting $[1,10^9]$.

title: Infinite Prime Nim losses
words: Prime Nim has infinitely many losing pile sizes (a known theorem, since primes have arbitrarily large gaps). Show they are rare.
math: Let $L=\{n: G(n)=0\}$ for the subtraction game with prime moves ($|L|=\infty$ is known). Prove $L$ has natural density $0$.

title: Square-sum coloring
words: Join numbers that add up to a perfect square. Does the number of colors needed stay bounded forever?
math: Decide whether $\sup_N \chi(S_N)<\infty$.

title: Lonely runners in 3D
words: Runners move in three dimensions on a cube that wraps around. Find the guaranteed loneliness.
math: For $n$ pairwise independent $v_i\in\mathbb{Z}^3$, find the optimal $\delta_n$ with $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|_{\mathbb{T}^3,\infty}\ge\delta_n$.

title: Hyperoperation at rank 2.5 is transcendental
words: Show 2 combined with 3 at "rank 2.5" in the natural hyperoperation family is transcendental.
math: For the unique natural family $a[s]b$, prove $2[2.5]3$ is transcendental.

title: Square-sum spanning trees
words: Show the square-sum graph has a spanning tree where no number connects to more than three others.
math: Prove that for all $N\ge 26$, $S_N$ has a spanning tree of maximum degree $3$.

title: Cube-sum connectivity
words: Join numbers that add to a perfect cube. Show everything links up once N is large.
math: Prove $C_N$ ($a\sim b\iff a+b$ is a cube) is connected for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Leaky firefighting
words: Fire spreads to each neighbour only with probability p. Find the largest p at which one firefighter per turn wins.
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with each burning–unburnt edge transmitting independently with probability $p$, find $p^*$ such that one protection per turn contains the fire a.s. iff $p<p^*$.

title: Real-rank hyperoperations
words: Addition, multiplication and exponentiation are ranks 1, 2, 3 of one ladder. Find natural rules that fix a unique operation at every real rank in between.
math: Find axioms (analytic in $s$, $a[s{+}1](b{+}1)=a[s](a[s{+}1]b)$, agreement with $+,\times,\uparrow$ at $s=1,2,3$) that determine $a[s]b$ uniquely for real $s\in[1,3]$, and prove uniqueness.

title: Square-sum Ramsey
words: Color the numbers 1 to N in two colors. Must there be a single-color pair adding to a square, triple, and so on?
math: Find the least $N$ such that every 2-colouring of $[N]$ has three numbers, pairwise summing to squares, in one colour.

title: Sofa beyond Gerver in 3 dimensions of turning
words: A 2D hallway that turns 90° twice in a row (an S-bend): find the best sofa.
math: Determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with two consecutive right turns in opposite directions, separated by length $L$, for every $L>0$.

title: Triangulated folding census
words: Count the ways to fold a small grid of triangles flat.
math: Count mountain–valley assignments on the $4\times4$ grid of squares cut by one diagonal each that are flat-foldable.

title: Smallest-odd-factor Collatz
words: Halve even numbers; send an odd number to the smallest odd prime dividing 3n + 1. Find every cycle that occurs below a billion.
math: Let $g(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even) and $g(n)=q(3n+1)$ ($n$ odd), $q$ the least odd prime factor ($1$ if none). Classify all cycles of $g$ meeting $[1,10^9]$.

title: Polykite structure theorem
words: Classify every shape of up to 20 kites: tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or fails within a few layers.
math: Prove each polykite with $\le20$ kites either tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or has Heesch number $\le10$.

title: Short Riemann
words: Shrink the 2026 machine-checked Riemann proof drastically.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of `RiemannHypothesis` in at most 10,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Square in a snowflake
words: Find the largest square whose four corners lie on the Koch snowflake.
math: Prove the Koch snowflake inscribes a square, and determine the maximal side length of an inscribed square.

title: Origami with a bounded number of layers
words: Find the best origami base for any tree when no point may have more than 4 layers of paper.
math: Give an algorithm for the minimal square paper for uniaxial bases of metric trees with layer count at most 4, with proof of optimality.

title: Hat magnets
words: Put a magnet on each hat tile. Show the system has a phase transition, and bound the critical temperature.
math: Prove the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat adjacency graph has $0<T_c<\infty$ with explicit two-sided bounds.
